new_claims.statement: If (S,U) has arbitrary joint density <=M, V is independent with scalar density <=N, a,b are nonzero, and h,R are arbitrary measurable functions, then Q=a(S-h(U))^2+R(U)+2b(U+alpha)(V+beta)+r0 has an essentially bounded density with ||p_Q||infinity <=3*2^(2/3)(MN)^(2/3)(|a|b^2)^(-1/3). The proof uses the exact one-sided half-Riesz potential of the square and does not require independence inside (S,U). Continuity is not claimed.

For a bounded dependent planar density Y, an independent bounded scalar V, and any nonsingular symmetric 3x3 carrier B=[[C,d],[d^T,0]], arbitrary planar quadratic curvature and affine terms are paid with ||p||infinity <=3*2^(2/3)(MN)^(2/3)|det B|^(-1/3), using an SL(2,R) planar change of variables that preserves density height.

For two projected coordinates from one original cap-one product bank and a scalar projection from a disjoint product bank, if the exact-rank-three carrier has zero scalar self-curvature, then ||p_(X^TAX)||infinity <=6*2^(2/3)|pdet A|^(-1/3). Under three nonzero eigenvalues of modulus at least one this is <=9.524406311809196.
